title: Debate Training Reduces Reward Hacking in RLAIF
abstract: arXiv:2608.17776v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: We demonstrate that RL finetuning an LLM using debate, a two-player adversarial game between a generator and a critic adjudicated by a weaker LLM judge, reduces reward hacking compared to a reinforcement learning from AI feedback (RLAIF) baseline. Reward hacking is a central obstacle in RLAIF: as training progresses, the policy learns to exploit systematic errors in its AI judge, degrading task performance, a problem that worsens precisely when the judge is weaker than the policy, the setting most relevant to overseeing increasingly capable AI systems. We study mathematics tasks, where final-answer correctness is verifiable, allowing us to measure reward hacking dynamics. We train a Gemini~2.5 Flash-class policy with a frozen, weaker Gemini~2.5 Flash Lite judge, comparing a single-player RLAIF baseline against debate. translated_title: 辩论训练减少RLAIF中的奖励黑客行为
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.17776v1 公告类型：新 摘要：我们证明，使用辩论（一种生成器与评论者之间的双人对抗游戏，由较弱的LLM裁判裁决）对LLM进行强化学习微调，相比基于AI反馈的强化学习（RLAIF）基线，能减少奖励黑客行为。奖励黑客是RLAIF中的核心障碍：随着训练进行，策略会学会利用其AI裁判的系统性错误，导致任务性能下降，而这一问题在裁判弱于策略时尤为严重，这恰恰是监督日益强大的AI系统最相关的情景。我们研究了数学任务，其中最终答案的正确性是可验证的，从而能够衡量奖励黑客的动态。我们使用冻结的、较弱的Gemini 2.5 Flash Lite裁判训练了一个Gemini 2.5 Flash类策略，比较了单玩家RLAIF基线与辩论方法。虽然基线迅速攻击裁判，但辩论在整个训练过程中保持了裁判性能，从而获得了更高的p
tldr: 本研究提出辩论训练方法，通过双人对抗游戏机制有效减少RLAIF中的奖励黑客行为，尤其在弱裁判监督强策略时，显著优于传统基线。
en_tdlr: This study proposes debate training, a two-player adversarial game mechanism that effectively reduces reward hacking in RLAIF, particularly when a weak judge oversees a strong policy, significantly outperforming the baseline.
